notes: Pupate (PUPATE): a tax on every trade in the launch pool buys Identity MD seats, puts them to work in the IMD swarm, lists them for resale, and burns PUPATE with the proceeds. TOKEN: PupateToken is a plain ERC-20, zero-argument constructor, 1e27 units minted to msg.sender (the factory), 18 decimals, burn and burnFrom only reduce supply, no owner, mint, pause, fee or limit. HOOK: PupateHook takes three constructor arguments: the chain's PoolManager, the sink (Cocoon, deployed before this launch at the address above) and the owner (an OpenZeppelin TimelockController with a 48-hour delay, at the address above). Address flags 0x18CC: afterInitialize, beforeAddLiquidity, beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta, afterSwapReturnDelta, validated by the constructor; it needs a mined CREATE2 salt. The first native-ETH pool initialised on the hook becomes the launch pool; deploy, initialise and seed in one transaction so no other pool can take that place. LIQUIDITY: beforeAddLiquidity admits liquidity only into the launch pool and only in the transaction that initialises it. afterInitialize sets a mark in transient storage (EIP-1153), which the EVM clears when that transaction ends, so the factory's own deploy, initialise and seed transaction is the only one that can ever add liquidity: a later transaction is refused even in the same block, and after the launch the pool's liquidity can only shrink. Removing liquidity is never gated. A test that seeds the pool must initialise it and add the liquidity in one call, as test/utils/PoolRouter.sol::open and script/local/LocalLaunchFactory.sol do. Known residual, kept on purpose and pinned by test_theOpeningTransactionIsTheGateNotTheAccountThatOpens: the mark names no account, so code that gets control later inside the opening transaction could add liquidity too; after it initialises the pool, the launch factory calls only the PoolManager, the launched token and its own registry in that transaction. test/fork/LaunchFactory.fork.t.sol rehearses the launch through the real launch factory on a mainnet fork. TAX: 6% of the ETH side of every buy and every sell in the launch pool, beside the pool's own LP fee, collected inside the swap as ERC-6909 claims (poolManager.mint); no ETH moves and no contract other than the PoolManager is called from a swap callback, so the first buy into a pool holding no ETH works. Exact-ETH swaps that cannot fill in full revert (PartialFill). For the first 93 minutes after the pool opens the buy tax starts at 99% and falls continuously by one percentage point a minute to 6%; sells always pay 6%. Swaps whose sender is the sink are untaxed (Cocoon's buybacks). flush() is permissionless: it converts the claims to ETH and calls Cocoon.depositTax with the hook's whole balance. The owner may only lower the standing tax (lowerTax) and transfer ownership; nothing can raise the tax, change the sink, or change the launch pool. TAX DESTINATION: Cocoon splits every deposit 85% to the strategy (seat pot and burn pot, by a mode the FloorFeed decides), 10% to the developer, 5% to buy and burn IMD. Vault ETH leaves only to Seaport (a seat purchase at or under the oracle floor plus 5%, the floor being the collection's lowest listing as a panel of IMD seats reads it), the PoolManager (a buyback bounded by a 5% price-impact limit), caller rewards of at most 1%, the developer balance, and the IMD auction's ETH lot. Cocoon, FloorFeed, PupateVesting and their tests are in this repository and were deployed before the launch; their addresses, the developer's 5% allocation (vested linearly over 12 months), the oracle question, and the timelock are documented in docs/deployment.md and README.md. POOL: currency0 native ETH, currency1 PUPATE, LP fee 12500 (the univ4_hook policy's tier), tick spacing 60, initialPrice sqrtPriceX96 for 1 ETH = 100,000,000 PUPATE (a 10 ETH valuation of the supply). REVIEW POINTS: the hook's sink and owner constants in the manifest; that nothing can raise the tax; the liquidity gate against the factory's own seeding transaction; test/PupateHook.t.sol, test/PupateHook.invariant.t.sol and test/cocoon/ against a real v4-core PoolManager. Three independent reviews are logged in docs/REVIEW.md; no audit or security claim is made. Nothing here is a statement about returns.
